parole.significato: To destroy (something); to ruin, to wreck.
parole.testo: Probably from Angloromani mul-, the preterite stem of mer- (“to die”) (compare mullered, mullo (“dead”, adjective); ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mer- (“to die; to disappear”)) + English -er (suffix forming frequentative verbs).

parole.significato: Badly damaged or completely destroyed; ruined, trashed, wrecked.
parole.testo: From muller (“to destroy; to beat or thrash; to utterly defeat or outplay”) + -ed (suffix forming past tense and past participle forms of regular verbs).
